claims.text: Combining high-energy mechanical alloying with rapid spark plasma sintering will produce a void-free W–Cu composite.
The combined process will produce a nanocrystalline W–Cu composite.
The processed composite will have improved microstructural uniformity relative to conventional Cu infiltration or prolonged sintering.
The processed composite will have improved mechanical durability under irradiation relative to conventional Cu infiltration or prolonged sintering.
High-energy ball milling followed by rapid spark plasma sintering is the proposed intervention for consolidating the W–Cu powder mixture.
The proposed SPS consolidation will be performed below the melting temperatures of both W and Cu.
A controlled atmosphere will minimize oxidation during processing.
The intervention will generate nanocrystalline W–Cu interfaces.
The intervention will enhance interparticle contact between W and Cu and minimize void formation.
Mechanical alloying refines the particle size of the W–Cu powder mixture.
Mechanical alloying cleans oxide layers from the W–Cu powders.
Mechanical alloying promotes intimate and chemically homogeneous mixing.
Applied pressure during SPS closes voids between powder-particle necks and shrinks the sample.
Rapid SPS consolidates the W–Cu powders before significant grain growth or void coalescence occurs.
The combined mechanism mitigates phase separation and defect formation in W–Cu.
Reduced void content and improved uniformity will enhance thermal transport in the W–Cu composite.
Reduced void content and improved uniformity will enhance mechanical durability under fusion-joint service conditions.
Conventional filling of a W skeleton with molten or powdered Cu, or sintering without prior mechanical alloying, typically produces phase separation and voids.
The proposed service boundary consists of high irradiation and thermal cycling conditions representative of fusion-reactor joints.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in void fraction and improvement in thermal and mechanical performance relative to the control will falsify the hypothesis.
